The image is a microscopic view showing fungal structures. Key observations:

- **Brown, septate hyphae** branching in the upper portion of the image
- **Two round/globose sporangia**: one on the left (brownish, irregular surface) and one on the right (dark/black, spherical) attached to a distinct sporangiophore
- The right structure shows a classic terminal spherical sporangium on a sporangiophore stalk
- The darkening/maturation of the sporangia is clearly visible

These microscopic features — sporangiophores bearing large, round, dark sporangia attached to brown hyphae — are diagnostic of **Rhizopus** species. Rhizopus soft rot is characterized by exactly this morphology: columellate sporangia on erect sporangiophores, with the sporangia turning dark/black at maturity.

This does not match Alternaria (which has muriform conidia), Sclerotinia (which forms sclerotia), or any bacterial disease class.
